title.narrative: Enhancing Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) Access as a Tool for Peacebuilding Phase 2.

description.narrative: This project aims to make water, sanitation, and hygiene services work better for everyone and last over time. It will help reduce open defecation in communities where sanitation is still very poor, while strengthening local leaders and WASH Committees to manage facilities in a fair, open, and responsible way. They will also gain skills to resolve disagreements peacefully and ensure that women, girls, and vulnerable people can use WASH facilities safely, with greater awareness of safeguarding and Sexual and Gender-Based Violence (SGBV) risks. The change we want to see is not only cleaner and healthier communities, but stronger and more united communities where shared resources are managed fairly, and conflicts are handled through dialogue rather than tension. The project targets 2300 households (approximately 13,800 individuals) in Kasuwan Ali, Sabon Gari, Bungha (Gyghat) and Pushit (Tilengpat) communities, with particular focus on 120 WASH Committees, 30 Water user committee (already established in Year one, which are included, persons with disability, women, men, and youth), low-income households with limited access to safe sanitation, 20 traditional and religious leaders to strengthen inclusive and conflict-sensitive WASH governance and Mangu LGA Chairman, WASH, Health, Social Welfare and National Orientation Agency Departments. These individuals play key roles in influencing behavior, resolving disputes, and managing WASH services The funding will support the deepening of integrated Peacebuilding and WASH interventions across the four communities of Bungha (Gyahat), Pushit (Tilengpat), Sabon Gari, and Kasuwan Ali. It will finance latrine construction in Sabon Gari and Kasuwan Ali, while consolidating hygiene promotion and community peacebuilding initiatives across all communities based on lessons from year one.
